To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the performance of a checkpoint and restart (CR) protocol depends on the application characteristics and (2) the performance of the protocol is not significantly affected by the system characteristics.

the performance of the checkpointing protocols depends on the characteristics (e.g., the number of processes, their execution times, the communication pattern, etc.) of the application and on the system and network characteristics.
the performance of checkpoint and recovery protocol varies with the application characteristics, the system on which the application is running, and the network on which it is communicating.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and analysis of a distributed process simulation environment that can be used for the performance evaluation of checkpoint and rollback recovery protocols in distributed applications.
the design and implementation issues of a checkpointing and recovery mechanism for distributed systems.
the design and analysis of fault-tolerant protocols for distributed systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of a protocol is dependent on the application, the system on which the application is run, and the network characteristics.

, in general, the performance of the protocols is not significantly affected by the system characteristics, but it is affected by the network characteristics and the characteristics of the applications.
the performance of the different checkpoint and recovery protocols is dependent on the application and system on which they are implemented and executed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dPSIM is a useful tool for evaluating performance of checkpoint and recovery techniques.
the performance of a checkpoint/recovery protocol is dependent on the application and system on which it is implemented.
we have designed, implemented and evaluated the performance of five checkpoint and rollback recovery protocols using dPSIM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the checkpoint and recovery protocols that are best for an application depend on the application characteristics and the system on the which it is running.
the checkpoint and rollback recovery protocol that is most suitable for a given application and system environment can be determined by using the simulation tool we have developed.
the performance of a checkpoint and rollback recovery protocol is a complex function of application and system parameters.
